reason: The text repeatedly demonstrates Yahweh actively working to help and liberate the Hebrew people from slavery. Yahweh insists on freeing them (שַׁלַּח אֶת־עַמִּי - 'let my people go'), protects them throughout the plagues by making distinctions between Goshen (where Hebrews live) and Egypt, preserves their livestock while Egypt's die, and institutes the Passover specifically to save Hebrew firstborns from death. Yahweh explicitly makes a covenant-based distinction: 'I will make a distinction on that day' (וְהִפְלֵיתִי בַיּוֹם הַהוּא). The text culminates with Yahweh striking Egypt's firstborn while 'passing over' Hebrew homes marked with blood, deliberately preserving Hebrew lives. These protective actions and liberation efforts represent a sustained commitment to helping the Hebrew people escape bondage.
